entradas.text: The historic Graf Manor lay on the outskirts of Arvory, at the end of a long, winding drive. Nearly two centuries old, it was as formidable as Lileas herself.
Lileas had invited me here for a private dinner, just the two of us.
I wasn't sure of her motivations, but was happy to have an excuse to escape the chaos back in Holsord.
I wasn't sure of her motivations, but I was happy to have an excuse to escape the unbearable loneliness at home.
I wasn't sure of her motivations. I only hoped I wouldn't have to spend the night there.
Serge dropped me off at the door.
I used the heavy brass door knocker to signal my arrival. The butler answered and showed me into the parlor.
entradas.menu: Knock.

entradas.text: I cautiously pushed the heavy door open. I followed the sound of classical music into the parlor.
entradas.menu: Go inside without knocking.

entradas.text: Gas lanterns lent the wood-paneled room a cosy orange glow. Lileas was sitting on the sofa. Above her hung a nearly life-sized portrait of a sallow, unhappy-looking young woman in a lace ball gown.
"Is that you?"
entradas.menu: "Is that you?"

entradas.text: "Is that your mother?"
entradas.menu: "Is that your mother?"

entradas.text: "Is that your grandmother?"
entradas.menu: "Is that your grandmother?"

entradas.text: Lileas nodded.
"My mother, actually."
"My mother, actually."
"I was her only child, you know. Giving birth to me left her medically unable to conceive."
"My father never could forgive her for not bearing him a son. And she never forgave me."
She took a measured sip of one of the two glasses of sparkling wine she was holding, and handed me the other.
"Sounds like a painful childhood."
entradas.menu: "Sounds like a painful childhood."

entradas.text: "Get to the point, Lileas. Why did you invite me here?"
entradas.menu: "Get to the point, Lileas. Why did you invite me here?"

entradas.text: "Given your current circumstances with Mrs. Rayne, I thought you could use a home-cooked supper."
"Given how your wife spends her time these days, I thought you might be in need of a home-cooked supper."
"I couldn't let you go a full term without having one of my home-cooked suppers."
The butler silently stepped into the parlor and rang a silver bell.
"The silver lining is that despite personally despising me, they felt compelled to grant me all the advantages a son would have had. Including the education I needed to rise to my current position."
"Ah. Speaking of which."

She led me into the dining room, where a glittering chandelier hung from the high ceiling. Beneath it was a long table set for two. A woman in an apron and chef's hat, Wehzek by her appearance, ceremoniously presented a roast rack of venison.
"Smells delicious."
entradas.menu: "Smells delicious."

entradas.text: "Nice story. Why am I here?"
entradas.menu: "Nice story. Why am I here?"

entradas.text: "Would you be so kind as to tell me why you invited me over?"
entradas.menu: "Would you be so kind as to tell me why you invited me over?"

entradas.text: "A home-cooked supper, huh?"
entradas.menu: "A home-cooked supper, huh?"

entradas.text: "Please, Mr. Rayne. I didn't get to where I am now by slaving away in the kitchen."
Lileas bowed her head and said a quick prayer, then motioned for me to dig in.
"The groundskeeper shot it this morning."
"Anton, I want you to know that I have nothing but respect for you."
"Thanks."
entradas.menu: "Thanks."

entradas.text: "I respect you too."
entradas.menu: "I respect you too."

entradas.text: "But?"
entradas.menu: "But?"

entradas.text: "But, given certain developments that have occurred over the course of your term, I believe you are no longer fit to lead the United Sordland Party."
"I wanted you to be the first to know that I myself will be running against you at the Party Congress."
"I forbid you from doing that."
entradas.menu: "I forbid you from doing that."

entradas.text: "What the hell do you mean, unfit?"
entradas.menu: "What the hell do you mean, unfit?"

entradas.text: "Are you going to pretend you're not currently on the verge of impeachment?"
"You're a disgrace to the memory of Tarquin Soll. Whom, lest we forget, you killed."
"You're a disgrace to the name of Tarquin Soll. Whom, lest we forget, you threw into prison."
"You're a disgrace to the name of Tarquin Soll. Whom, lest we forget, you tried to have imprisoned."
I spat a mouthful of chewed-up venison across the table.
entradas.menu: Spit out your food in shock.

entradas.text: "Did you think I'd sit by as you made a mockery out of this country's constitution?"
"Did you think I'd sit by after you ignored our request to seize power from the Oligarchs?"
"You're a disgrace to the good name of Tarquin Soll."
Lileas took a deep breath.
"I don't know why you're surprised."
"Don't play dumb with me."
"And who are you to give me orders?"
"Did you poison my food?"
entradas.menu: "Did you poison my food?"

entradas.text: "It's a little late for that."
"You're fired."
entradas.menu: "You're fired."

entradas.text: "How much money will it take for you to stay on my side?"
entradas.menu: "How much money will it take for you to stay on my side?"

entradas.text: Lileas gave a short laugh and gestured at our grand surroundings.
"Do I look like I need money?"
Lileas reached over to my plate, took a forkful of meat and ate it while looking me in the eye.
"I don't need those kinds of tricks to beat you."
"I'm doing you a courtesy tonight. I didn't want to surprise you at the Congress."
"And I wanted to give you time to consider backing me."
"You're mad."
entradas.menu: "You're mad."

entradas.text: "Sorry, Lileas. I can't back down now."
entradas.menu: "Sorry, Lileas. I can't back down now."

entradas.text: "I won't do it. And neither will the rest of the party."
entradas.menu: "I won't do it. And neither will the rest of the party."

entradas.text: "We'll see about that."
She smiled mysteriously.
"I understand."
"That's what they said about you, when you first went up against Alphonso."
"I'll tender my official resignation once we're both back in Holsord."
I rose from my chair.
"It's a shame to lose you."
entradas.menu: "It's a shame to lose you."

entradas.text: "May the best man win, then."
entradas.menu: "May the best man win, then."

entradas.text: "I understand now why you never found a husband."
entradas.menu: "I understand now why you never found a husband."

entradas.text: "Likewise."
"I'll have the butler show you out."
She stayed seated as her butler gently led me outside.
As Serge and I drove away, I looked in the rearview mirror and saw her silhouette in the doorway.
So I was being challenged from within my own party. At least Lileas wouldn't pose much of a threat.
Or so I hoped.
"Mr. President, I wish I had been consulted on this military parade decision. Is that really the best use of our time and resources given the mounting unrest in this country?"
"Don't worry. The military's taking care of it."
entradas.menu: "Don't worry. The military's taking care of it."

entradas.text: "Aren't your police taking care of it?"
entradas.menu: "Aren't your police taking care of it?"

entradas.text: "The police are taking care of it. A little too well, I might add."
entradas.menu: "The police are taking care of it. A little too well, I might add."

entradas.text: "The military's taking care of it. A little too well, actually."
entradas.menu: "The military's taking care of it. A little too well, actually."

entradas.text: "I've got it all under control."
entradas.menu: "I've got it all under control."

entradas.text: "I worked things out diplomatically. Like I said I would."
entradas.menu: "I worked things out diplomatically. Like I said I would."

entradas.text: "For now. But now that you've shown you're willing to negotiate, these people will never be happy."
"You and I both know that's not true. Your 'diplomacy' was a disaster."
"They'd be doing a lot better if you hadn't fired my best man."
"You gave them authority to act within Sordland's borders. Whatever they do is on your head."
"You gave the orders. You can't blame them for doing their job."
"That itself is cause for worry."
"They're doing their best. But Sordland is far from safe."
"Mr. President, I'm worried the mounting unrest might hurt our chances of re-election."
"Lies. All lies."
entradas.menu: "Lies. All lies."

entradas.text: "Those scandal revelations about you are circulating in the government circles and might soon spread further out..."
"The encroaching war with Rumburg certainly doesn't help matters."
"I'll be just fine."
entradas.menu: "I'll be just fine."

entradas.text: "What do you think I should do about that?"
entradas.menu: "What do you think I should do about that?"

entradas.text: I grabbed my fork.
entradas.menu: Start eating.

entradas.text: "Aren't you forgetting something?"
It was some of the best meat I'd ever had. We ate in silence for a while, then Lileas pensively laid down her cutlery.
"I don't think the allegations will do much damage, but it's worth keeping an eye on."
"A strong leader would ignore the allegations and focus on winning the election. By all means necessary."
"Don't be silly. Karl told me everything."
"I'm sure they are."
"Anton, thank you for all the help you've given to my ministry during your term."
"You followed through on your campaign promises, and Sordland is stronger and safer for it."
"I'm all the more grateful considering it wasn't even initially a priority of yours."
"Anton, I wish you had made national security more of a top priority during your term."
"Especially considering you were voted in on your promise to focus on it."
"But I was thrilled when you recognized Sordish schools' right to religious expression over Ms. Walda's ridiculous objections."
"And I regret that you caved to Ms. Walda and mandated the teaching of that evolution nonsense in schools."
"In any event, I'm looking forward to working more closely together during your next term."
"Regardless, I'm looking forward to working more closely together during your next term."
"I was thrilled when you recognized Sordish schools' right to religious expression over Ms. Walda's ridiculous objections."
"I do regret that you caved to Ms. Walda and mandated the teaching of that evolution nonsense in schools."
"Karl deserved it."
entradas.menu: "Karl deserved it."

entradas.text: "Sorry about that. I had to make an example out of him."
entradas.menu: "Sorry about that. I had to make an example out of him."

entradas.text: "As long as you can call off your dogs when the time comes."
entradas.menu: "As long as you can call off your dogs when the time comes."

entradas.text: "As long as the threats are neutralized."
entradas.menu: "As long as the threats are neutralized."

entradas.text: "If Iosef turns against me, that could mean trouble for all of us."
entradas.menu: "If Iosef turns against me, that could mean trouble for all of us."

entradas.text: "As long as Iosef is still on my side, they won't get out of hand."
entradas.menu: "As long as Iosef is still on my side, they won't get out of hand."

entradas.text: "I know what you think I should've done. But the police would only make a mess of things."
entradas.menu: "I know what you think I should've done. But the police would only make a mess of things."

entradas.text: "What would you have me do, shoot the lot of them?"
entradas.menu: "What would you have me do, shoot the lot of them?"

entradas.text: Lileas pursed her lips.
"I don't think the allegations will do much damage, especially with your opposition so weakened. But it's worth keeping an eye on."
"Thanks for everything you've done, Lileas."
entradas.menu: "Thanks for everything you've done, Lileas."

entradas.text: "Don't worry about me. Focus on doing your job."
entradas.menu: "Don't worry about me. Focus on doing your job."

entradas.text: Lileas nodded.
"Me too, if it means more excellent dinners like this."
entradas.menu: "Me too, if it means more excellent dinners like this."

entradas.text: "And placing the Gendarmerie under my jurisdiction was above and beyond my highest expectations."
"I do wish you had heeded my request to place the Gendarmerie under my jurisdiction."
"But I'm pleased you at least recognized the need to place the Gendarmerie under my jurisdiction."
"Likewise, I wish you had heeded my request to place the Gendarmerie under my jurisdiction."
"Not to mention feeling the need to pump our children full of strange chemicals in response to some unconfirmed health threat."
"However, I'm grateful you defended Sordish citizens' right not to subject their children to mandatory vaccinations."
"Likewise, I'm grateful you defended Sordish citizens' right not to subject their children to mandatory vaccinations."
"I was less enthused about your decision to pump our children full of strange chemicals in response to some unconfirmed health threat."
"I'll drink to that."
entradas.menu: "I'll drink to that."

entradas.text: "God willing."
entradas.menu: "God willing."

entradas.text: We clinked glasses.
Lileas raised her glass and smiled.
Lileas' upper lip twitched, but she remained calm.
"How are you feeling about that, may I ask?"
"How are you feeling about the encroaching war with Rumburg?"
"Great. We'll show those snobs who's boss."
entradas.menu: "Great. We'll show those snobs who's boss."

entradas.text: "Not terrific, to be honest. I didn't want a war during my presidency."
entradas.menu: "Not terrific, to be honest. I didn't want a war during my presidency."

entradas.text: "How are you feeling about it?"
entradas.menu: "How are you feeling about it?"

entradas.text: "Nobody does, dear."
"I'm glad you're feeling positive."
"From a national security perspective, quite good. We've managed to keep a lid on any potential intelligence leaks."
"From a national security perspective, I think we're in good shape. We've managed to keep a lid on any potential intelligence leaks."
"To be honest, I'm a little worried. Our national security's still shaky. There may be information leaking to Rumburg from within the Maroon Palace."
"I'm a little worried myself. Our national security's still shaky. There may be information leaking to Rumburg from within the Maroon Palace."
"Since imprisoning my ex-secretary, you mean."
entradas.menu: "Since imprisoning my ex-secretary, you mean."

entradas.text: "If only the other ministries were as prepared as yours."
entradas.menu: "If only the other ministries were as prepared as yours."

entradas.text: "So Livia was acting alone."
entradas.menu: "So Livia was acting alone."

entradas.text: "Keep up the good work."
entradas.menu: "Keep up the good work."

entradas.text: "I'm sure you'll find the source."
entradas.menu: "I'm sure you'll find the source."

entradas.text: "Maybe Lucian was right about Livia."
entradas.menu: "Maybe Lucian was right about Livia."

entradas.text: "Exactly."
"It appears so."
"Thank you for your vote of confidence."
"Maybe?"
"Never mind."
entradas.menu: "Never mind."

entradas.text: "We'll talk about that later."
entradas.menu: "We'll talk about that later."

entradas.text: Lileas paused. She fixed me with a piercing look.
"Remember, war requires sacrifices. I hope you're ready to do what it takes."
Livia frowned, then looked up and looked me straight in the eye.
"Especially with dear Franc in the military."
"Franc wants to fight. He'll do anything for this country."
entradas.menu: "Franc wants to fight. He'll do anything for this country."

entradas.text: "I'm not sending Franc to the front lines."
entradas.menu: "I'm not sending Franc to the front lines."

entradas.text: "Franc would be useless in a war."
entradas.menu: "Franc would be useless in a war."

entradas.text: "That's good to hear. I think back so fondly on my own military days."
"Come, now. Give the boy a chance to do his country and his father proud."
"Of course I am."
entradas.menu: "Of course I am."

entradas.text: "We'll win this without having to sacrifice a damn thing."
entradas.menu: "We'll win this without having to sacrifice a damn thing."

entradas.text: "Good."
"Language!"
We ate silently for a little while longer, then Lileas spoke up again.
By the end of the meal, I was pleasantly full and a little tipsy. The butler had to lead me back through the manor's winding corridors until I found the door.
I waved at Lileas out the window as Serge pulled away. The coming campaign would be turbulent, but at least I had her on my side.
"Did you think I liked it when you refused to tighten Sordland's borders against disreputable migrants?"
"Was I really going to ignore your foolish refusal to re-instate conscription?"
"Even if you weren't steering this party further and further from its roots..."
"Even if you hadn't unceremoniously deposed honorable Supreme Court justices to suit your own perverse purposes..."
"Just stay true to your promise to honor our party's conservative roots, and the good Lord will take care of the rest."
"Enough of this. Lileas, I know about your role in the Bernard Circas murder."
entradas.menu: "Enough of this. Lileas, I know about your role in the Bernard Circas murder."

entradas.text: Lileas calmly sipped her wine.
"I'm sure I have no idea what you're talking about."
"No? Maybe you should ask Orso Hawker. He's being held over at the Justice Ministry right now."
entradas.menu: "No? Maybe you should ask Orso Hawker. He's being held over at the Justice Ministry right now."

entradas.text: "No? Maybe you should ask Orso Hawker and Heron Garaci. They're being held over at the Justice Ministry right now."
entradas.menu: "No? Maybe you should ask Orso Hawker and Heron Garaci. They're being held over at the Justice Ministry right now."

entradas.text: "Maybe you should ask half of the deep state that was purged. I only spared you because you're more valuable on my side."
entradas.menu: "Maybe you should ask half of the deep state that was purged. I only spared you because you're more valuable on my side."

entradas.text: Lileas' face hardened.
"What do you want, Anton?"
"For you not to run against me, obviously. You'll join me on the campaign trail. Enthusiastically."
entradas.menu: "For you not to run against me, obviously. You'll join me on the campaign trail. Enthusiastically."

entradas.text: "Well, now that I know you've been planning to betray me, I want to see you brought to justice. I'm ordering your arrest tomorrow."
entradas.menu: "Well, now that I know you've been planning to betray me, I want to see you brought to justice. I'm ordering your arrest tomorrow."

entradas.text: Lileas grimaced.
"Very well, Mr. President."
Lileas glared at me.
"Now get out of my house."
"Get out of my house."
"Thanks for dinner."
entradas.menu: "Thanks for dinner."

entradas.text: "With pleasure."
entradas.menu: "With pleasure."

entradas.text: Without waiting for the butler to show me out, I rose from my seat and made my way to the front door.
She would make a formidable enemy. I was happy to have corralled her to my side.
As Serge and I drove away, I looked in the rear-view mirror and saw her silhouette in the doorway.
For now, at least.
She would make a formidable enemy. Thanks to my investigation, I'd managed to dodge that bullet.
"It's over Lileas and you know it. There is no need to make it worse."
entradas.menu: "It's over Lileas and you know it. There is no need to make it worse."

entradas.text: "Our borders were open to an influx of subversives and refugees that overwhelmed Bergia due to your inability to secure our borders to the west."
"The very constitution that is keeping this nation safe from internal and external threats."
"I suspected that might happen."
entradas.menu: "I suspected that might happen."

entradas.text: "Of course you did. You aren't stupid."
"Give me some time to think about it."
entradas.menu: "Give me some time to think about it."

entradas.text: "I will take my leave. Thanks for the evening nonetheless."
entradas.menu: "I will take my leave. Thanks for the evening nonetheless."

entradas.text: "Those leaked scandal revelations certainly haven't helped matters..."
